# easing.library: EvaluateMirrored

**Status:** Supported (tier `graphics`). In a shipping tier; the lint, type-check, and code-generation gates cover it. No release promises its signature yet.

## Summary

> The playback-reversed curve sampled at t: f(1 - t), which runs from 1 down
> to 0 as t goes 0 to 1 (the source curve played backwards).

## Signature

```plato
EvaluateMirrored(self: IEasingFunction, t: Number): Number
```

## Laws

These are declared laws. Whether each one passes is recorded by the law runner ([stdlib/VERIFICATION.md](../../../../../stdlib/VERIFICATION.md)), not by this page.

### Law_MirroredIsEvalOfComplementaryTime

[stdlib/tests/easing.laws.plato, line 36](../../../../../stdlib/tests/easing.laws.plato#L36)

```plato
// Mirrored playback samples the same curve at the complementary time.
Law_MirroredIsEvalOfComplementaryTime(f: IEasingFunction, t: Number): Boolean
    => f.EvaluateMirrored(t).LawEq(f.Eval(1.0 - t));
```

### Law_ReversedIsComplementOfMirrored

[stdlib/tests/easing.laws.plato, line 40](../../../../../stdlib/tests/easing.laws.plato#L40)

```plato
// The ease-in to ease-out transform is the complement of mirrored playback.
Law_ReversedIsComplementOfMirrored(f: IEasingFunction, t: Number): Boolean
    => f.EvaluateReversed(t).LawEq(1.0 - f.EvaluateMirrored(t));
```
